newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended higher across the board on fund buying. The was little or no roaster interest as the market made its way higher. The fact that the Brazilian government coffee auction of 120,100 bags of stocks was completely sold out was taken as a sign that the domestic market is exceptionally tight, implying that there is little coffee available for export at present. However, December shipments proved to be stronger than expected. In New York arabica futures ended mixed in uneventful dealings. Producers selling is likely to continue to limit gains, which appear to have been mostly speculative oriented. Traders said high Brazilian exports at a time when Central American shipments are also expected to rise could put some downward pressure on the market. March added 45 points to close at 119.35 cents/lb while May closed 55 points higher at 117.15 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - Brazil's green coffee exports for December 1996 will weigh-in at around 1.55 million 60-kg bags, according to the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation (FEBEC). It was added that December shipments have proven stronger than expected and that the total of 1.55 million bags would bring Brazilian exports very close to its quota under the ACPC retention scheme. Brazil agreed to export no more than 9 million bags through July/December 1996 and 6 million bags through January/June 1997. Brazil's July/November exports totalled 7.44 million bags.

EL SALVADOR - According to the executive director of the Salvadoran Coffee Council, Ruben Pineda, coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) will reach 2.346 million 60-kg bags, down 5 percent from the quantity produced the previous year. The low output was ascribed to rains that damaged trees early in 1996. Pineda said the study was carried out in 16,000 farms throughout the country. However the chairwoman of the Salvadoran Coffee Association, the country's producer group, disagreed. Elena Bolanos said production would fall by 230,000 60-kg bags this season. She added El Salvador's output in 1995/96 was around 2.453 million 60-kg bags which would mean a crop of around 2.2 million bags in 1996/97. She said winds and rain had caused the dip in production, especially affecting high-altitude coffee growing regions.

FRANCE - France imported 620,147 bags of coffee in October 1996, 9.3 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 5.672 million bags, 7 percent more in the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.5 percent to 6.246 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Ivory Coast (663,700 vs 645,100 bags), Uganda (449,100 vs 332,600 bags), Brazil (616,200 vs 754,700 bags) and Colombia (469,900 vs 440,800 bags). The country exported 1.005 million bags of coffee in January/October 1996, nearly 14 percent more than in the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar 1995 fell 7 percent to 1.074 million bags.
